* [[Chile]]'s [[Supreme Court of Chile|Supreme Court]] strips former military ruler [[Augusto Pinochet]] of his immunity from prosecution, allowing him to be prosecuted for alleged crimes including involvement in murder and [[torture]]. [http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/world/americas/3602630.stm (BBC)]
* [[Iraqi resistance#Rebellion in Najaf .28August 2004.29|Najaf standoff]]
** Twenty-five people are killed and 100 wounded during a [[mortar (weapon)|mortar]] attack on the main [[mosque]] in the [[Iraq]]i city of [[Kufa]]. 20 [[Shiite]] marchers in Kufa are killed and 70 wounded by gunfire. The identity of the attackers is unknown, reportedly though a source of gunfire was near an [[Iraqi National Guard]] base. [http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/world/middle_east/3600384.stm (BBC)] [https://www.reuters.com/newsArticle.jhtml?type=worldNews&storyID=6078307 (Reuters)]{{Dead link|date=August 2021 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} [http://www.cnn.com/2004/WORLD/meast/08/26/iraq.main/index.html (CNN)] [http://www.albawaba.com/news/index.php3?sid=283760&lang=e&dir=news (Albawaba)]
** [[Ayatollah|Grand Ayatollah]] [[Grand Ayatollah Ali al-Sistani|Ali al-Sistani]] begins negotiations with [[Shiite]] [[cleric]] [[Moqtada al-Sadr]] in a bid to end the fighting in [[Najaf]] for three weeks. Sistani tells thousands of Iraqis heading to the [[holy city]] to wait on the outskirts of Najaf. [https://web.archive.org/web/20141110214559/http://www.khaleejtimes.com/DisplayArticle.asp?xfile=data%2Ffocusoniraq%2F2004%2FAugust%2Ffocusoniraq_August292.xml&section=focusoniraq (khaleejtimes)] Ayatollah Sistani calls a pause in fighting, telling protesters to stay home, and urging all forces to withdraw. US and Iraqi troops suspend attacks for 24 hours. [http://www.csmonitor.com/2004/0827/p01s01-woiq.html (CSMonitor)] [https://www.reuters.com/newsArticle.jhtml?type=topNews&storyID=6082585 (Reuters)] {{Webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20040827055838/http://www.reuters.com/newsArticle.jhtml?type=topNews&storyID=6082585 |date=2004-08-27 }}
* [[Abu Hamza al-Masri]], a well known Muslim cleric currently residing in the United Kingdom, is arrested under the [[Terrorism Act 2000]] which covers the "commission, preparation or instigation of acts of [[terrorism]]". [https://www.reuters.com/newsArticle.jhtml?type=worldNews&storyID=6081021 (Reuters)] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050122053351/http://www.reuters.com/newsArticle.jhtml?type=worldNews&storyID=6081021 |date=2005-01-22 }}
